patterns_learned: Week B (News+Academic) consistently produces academic papers as the most reliable source type — major news sources are largely blocked by bot detection
Paper titles themselves serve as source confirmation when the camera name appears in the title (as with WSL paper)
SAGE and ScienceDirect both block WebFetch but are confirmed via search snippet fragments
AP/wire service photography stories are very hard to verify: brand-specific camera names often stripped in intermediary coverage
Formal brand partnerships (e.g. Antigravity x Insta360) are disqualified even if not on exclusion list — must be genuinely undiscovered
Recency flag needed: some academic papers published 2025 report fieldwork from 2023 — flag for human reviewer
Multiple independent search snippet confirmations (3+) are sufficient for camera brand verification when WebFetch blocked
week_c_suggestions: Reddit: r/insta360, r/360video, r/videography — look for active threads Oct 2024-present with first-person use
Vimeo: search 'insta360' with filter date:2024-2026, Staff Picks or niche channels
YouTube: small channels (<10k subscribers) with recent insta360 tutorials or field use
GitHub/academic repos: look for datasets or code referencing Insta360 cameras
Google Groups / specialist listservs for archaeology, ecology, emergency response
feedback: Week B searches surface academic papers well — lean into Google Scholar + doi.org patterns
When paper title itself contains camera name, that is sufficient for Verification Check #1
Drop stories where brand cannot be confirmed directly (AP sled dog story: correct call to drop)
Low-Medium confidence stories should still be included with clear flags — human reviewer can decide
403 blocks are not failures — use search snippets as primary evidence when multiple fragments agree
